Wall time 520 min vs v8's 522 min. Because the DFS also carries a 60 s per-predict time budget, a wider bound does not necessarily cost more wall-clock; it reallocates the same budget across a broader, shallower frontier. This is a confound: a null result cannot distinguish 'bound was not binding' from 'wider bound explored more but ran out of time budget'. If v9 scores flat, the next lever should separate these (raise dfs_time_budget_seconds at the widened bound, or measure candidate-set size directly in an offline probe) before abandoning the recall hypothesis.
